title: Jamia students start hunger strike for union elections
seoTitle: Delhi Jamia students hunger strike for union poll

tea.why: Jamia Millia Islamia students are protesting because student union elections have not been held at the university since 2006.
tea.want: Protesters demand the restoration of student union elections, an independent election commission, and an Internal Complaints Committee.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Five students were on an indefinite hunger strike after moving their protest to Ghalib Lawn near Gate 7.

summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi launched an indefinite hunger strike to demand the reinstatement of student union elections, which have been suspended since 2006 due to past concerns over discipline and violence. The demonstration started with three students and grew to five, with participants drawing inspiration from a successful hunger strike at Aligarh Muslim University. In addition to union polls, protesters called for an independent election commission and a properly constituted Internal Complaints Committee to address sexual harassment. A university spokesperson stated that the administration has not opposed unions in principle but had not received a written representation, adding that department-wise representatives have worked better historically to prevent excessive politicisation and clashes.
demands: Establish an independent election commission for the union
response: A university spokesperson stated they had not received anything in writing from the students and noted that past experiences favored department-wise representatives over politicised union systems. Protesters also alleged that Delhi Police escorted them away from Gate 18 and detained some students.

updates.text: The indefinite hunger strike began with three students before growing to five participants.
Protesters relocated to Ghalib Lawn near Gate 7 after police allegedly escorted them away from Gate 18 and detained some participants.
